answer: Mixing-time analysis resists sybils: an honest trust graph is fast-mixing — a random walk spreads quickly across the whole atlas of nodes — but a sybil region joined by a thin cut is slow-mixing, trapping walks on its own island far longer than chance allows. Measuring how fast walks disperse flags the fakes: their internal vine of edges cannot hide the bottleneck that slows mixing into and out of their cluster. Influence granted only to fast-mixing regions starves the trapped sybils.
